_comment: Proof cells for the gf180mcu DRC bring-up (issue #15), and what each one
is expected to make `klt drc` say. run_drc.py runs every cell listed here
and FAILS the run if the report's rule_counts do not match `expect`
exactly -- that assertion is the whole point: it is what distinguishes a
green bring-up from a DRC pass that never checked anything.
generator  script that (re)builds `gds`, run with an interpreter that
has the pip `klayout` package. Committed alongside the GDS so
the proof survives an upstream deck change.
gds        committed GDSII stream, byte-reproducible (the generators
below is a real integrity check.
expect     exact {rule id: count} the JSON report's `rule_counts` must
equal. `{}` means the report must be status=clean.
expect_status  redundant with `expect` but stated so a reader does not
Keep `expect` in sync with each generator's SEEDED_VIOLATIONS dict.

Cells whose `gds`/`generator` paths reach outside this directory are the block-level layout of issue #57 (layout/adc-top/). They are listed here, rather than in a second runner, so every DRC result this repo has lands in one append-only record trail with one set of assertions. Each expects `clean` -- and as of the issue #70 pin bump that `clean` finally covers the MiM capacitor stack too: the deck now carries MIMTM.1/.2/.3 and Metal2/3/5/MetalTop rules (klayout-tools#188/#189, closed upstream), so `adc_cdac_cell`/`adc_top`/`adc_block` reporting clean is a checked result over their 1224-per-block unit-capacitor footprints and not an unchecked one. What a clean report here still does NOT cover is stated in layout/adc-top/README.md.

cells.name: sw_unit
cells.role: positive control -- a single switch device on the four covered layers, carrying two seeded violations

cells.name: uncovered_layer_probe
cells.role: former negative control -- RE-BASELINED at the issue #70 toolchain-pin bump, which is the event this cell was built to detect. It draws grossly illegal geometry on the MiM stack (Metal4/FuseTop/Via4/Metal5) and on Metal2/Metal3, all of which the deck had no rules for at the previous pin, so it reported `clean` and that `clean` WAS the coverage gap. The pinned deck now checks every one of those layers and catches it. The rule ids below are the closure, recorded rather than the gap; three of the four failures gen_uncovered_layer_probe.py's docstring predicted are now caught by name (MIMTM.1 = mim.space.1, MIMTM.3 = mim.enclosing.fusetop.1, plus the sub-minimum Metal2/Metal3 widths). The fourth, MIMTM.2 = mim.enclosing.via4.1, is IN the deck and is evaluated (it is absent from the report's rules_skipped) but does not fire here: it is scoped to the derived 'virtual bottom plate' (FuseTop sized by 1.06 um, intersected with Metal4), and this probe's FuseTop hangs entirely off its Metal4, so the via straddles an edge of a region the derived layer does not cover. Confirmed not to be a deck defect by a separate scratch probe drawn as a well-formed MiM stack with only the Via4 overlap wrong, which the same rule catches -- see the record for this run

cells.name: adc_drv
cells.role: leaf cell: local T-gate driver (`adc_drv`), from design/adc-top/adc_top.spice -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: adc_tgate
cells.role: leaf cell: CDAC bottom-plate decode T-gate (`adc_tgate`, 10u/20u) -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: adc_tgate_dum
cells.role: leaf cell: input sampling switch (`adc_tgate_dum`, DR-0007/DR-0013 dummy-compensated T-gate) -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: adc_cdac_cell
cells.role: leaf cell: one CDAC weighted-position cell (4 decode T-gates -- DR-0014's fourth, one-hot leg to `vin` included -- 4 local drivers, one unit MiM cap footprint) -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: adc_tp_sw
cells.role: leaf cell: top-plate V_cm switch (adc_tp_sw, DR-0014: one local driver plus one CDAC-geometry T-gate) -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: comparator
cells.role: comparator cell: 27 transistors plus the two common-centroid 150 kohm poly load resistors -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: comparator_nores
cells.role: comparator cell without the resistor bodies -- the companion LVS case that keeps pop/pon distinct -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: adc_top
cells.role: BLOCK: everything design/adc-top/adc_top.spice defines -- two CDAC array sides (1024 common-centroid unit caps + dummy rings), their decode banks, the two per-side top-plate V_cm switches (DR-0014), guard rings and the reserved SAR-logic region -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: adc_block
cells.role: BLOCK: the assembled block -- adc_top plus the comparator, strapped to the top plates and the analog rails -- expected DRC-clean, but see layout/README.md and layout/adc-top/README.md: the deck covers only Comp/Poly2/Contact/Metal1/Nwell, so a clean report says NOTHING about the MiM capacitor stack

cells.name: adc_cdac_array
cells.role: PROOF CELL (issue #81): one side of the CDAC array drawn device=True -- 512 recognised unit MiM caps plus the per-weight Metal4->Via3->Metal3->Via2->Metal2->Via1->Metal1 bottom-plate interconnect that ties each weight's scattered units to its own trunk pin. Unlike the block cells above, a clean report here IS a checked result over the new Metal2/Metal3 interconnect AND the MiM stack (mim.enclosing.fusetop.1/.via4.1, mim.space.1, metal2/3.width.1) -- the drawn interconnect that lets the array's caps become extractable devices at all
